title: Is coredns misconfigured in the kubespray v2.21.0? The service always times out, but node ips from the service work fine.
body:
I realise that this problem might be in kubespray, calico, coredns or me, so I've added this as a question rather than a bug. 

I've deployed k8s 1.25.6 with kubespray v2.21.0, using calico, coredns and nodelocaldns. The coredns config is this:

```
    .:53 {
        errors
        health {
            lameduck 5s
        }
        ready
        kubernetes cluster.local in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa {
          pods insecure
          fallthrough in-addr.arpa ip6.arpa
        }
        prometheus :9153
        forward . /etc/resolv.conf {
          prefer_udp
          max_concurrent 1000
        }
        cache 30

        loop
        reload
        loadbalance
    }
```
For the record the host `/etc/resolv.conf` is identical on all nodes, and contain my network dns and the nodelocaldns address as nameservers like so:

```
nameserver 169.254.25.10
nameserver 10.30.1.1
search fet
```

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> For the record the host /etc/resolv.conf is identical on all nodes, and contain my network dns **and the nodelocaldns address** as nameservers like so:

This is problematic. Nodelocaldns sends non-cluster domain queries to the upstream servers listed in `/etc/resolv.conf`.  If one of those servers is the nodelocaldns address itself, then you've created a partial forwarding loop, where nodelocaldns has a 50% chance of forwarding any non-cluster domain query to itself.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Right that makes sense and a loop here sounds bad. So I went ahead and replaced the symlink to the systemd generated resolv.conf which was currently inplace for all my nodes and instead created an new file without the nodelocaldns nameserver listing. 

The thing though is that after changeing this, restarting coredns pods and nodelocaldns pods they both still have the nodelocaldns listed as one of two nameservers. 

ahh, that is coming from the kubelet-config:
`resolvConf: /run/systemd/resolve/resolv.conf`

No idea why participant2.254.25.10 is being added by systemd though. 

But even after updating the kublet-config, restarting the kubelet service, the coredns pods and nodelocaldns pods they all have participant2.254.25.10 as a second nameserver. And the nodelocaldns pods are still logging the timeout errors.

comments.body:
Yeah I did a restart of both coredns and nodelocaldns pods after restarting the kubelet. And I just verified that the /etc/resolv.conf has not been changed since I updated it. But running `systemd-resolve --status` on a master node gives:

```
Global

    resolv.conf mode: foreign
         DNS Servers: participant2.254.25.10
Fallback DNS Servers: 10.30.1.1
```

So somehow, both my network DNS and the nodelocaldns are "loaded" eventhough the nodelocaldns is not listed in /etc/resolve.conf anymore. This is even after a reboot of the master node. 

But I did found this: https://<redacted-host>/questions/515154/how-do-you-remove-bad-dns-server-ips-from-systemd-resolved
Which showed me how to add my Network DNS server, and led me to find `/etc/systemd/resolved.conf` which for some reason had the nodelocaldns ip set as main DNS. Removing that, and reloading systemd-resolved finally gave my nodelocaldns pods the correct /etc/resolve.conf. 

However, nodelocaldns pods are still logging the errors on timeouts reaching 10.133.0.3:53. xD

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Okay, so it turns out that calico and nodelocaldns will compete for iptables configuration, and calico eventually always wins. I've made a change to the  FelixConfiguration adding a `chainInsertMode: Append` and now the iptable rules from nodelocaldns seems to stick around. I can access the coredns service from all nodes so all should be well. But still, there just as many timouts. And it seems to me that what's happening is that the coreos pod is taking longer than 2 seconds to reply the first time it sees a domain query. I tested this myself and most non-cached domains timeout after 2 seconds, but succeeded if I set the timeout to 5 seconds. Any pointers on digging further into that would be great.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
So I started googling for this 1m timeout. Came across this: https://github.com/projectcalico/calico/issues/3145
Turns out that the fix is nothing but `sudo ethtool --offload vxlan.calico rx off tx off`. And boom. Problem is completely and instantly gone.
